orig_commit_message:
[FLINK-37446][table-api-java] Support named arguments in Table API

This closes #26282.
improved_commit_message: Add support for named arguments in function calls
change_summary: This commit introduces named arguments functionality in the SQL and Table API. Named arguments allow users to provide arguments to functions without worrying about their order, improving readability and usability, especially when dealing with functions with many parameters.
hints: Introduced a new method asArgument for creating named arguments.
Updated function signatures to support named argument binding.
Enhanced type inference to accommodate named arguments.
Covered functionality with extensive test cases to ensure robustness.

@@ -230,3 +230,42 @@ table
 {{< /tabs >}}
 
 {{< top >}}
+
+Named Arguments
+---------------------------------------
+
+By default, values and expressions are mapped to a function's arguments based on the position in the function call,
+for example `f(42, true)`. All functions in both SQL and Table API support position-based arguments.
+
+If the function declares a static signature, named arguments are available as a convenient alternative.
+The framework is able to reorder named arguments and consider optional arguments accordingly, before passing them
+into the function call. Thus, the order of arguments doesn't matter when calling a function and optional arguments
+don't have to be provided.
+
+In `DESCRIBE FUNCTION` and documentation a static signature is indicated by the `=>` assignment operator,
+for example `f(left => INT, right => BOOLEAN)`. Note that not every function supports named arguments. Named
+arguments are not available for signatures that are overloaded, use varargs, or any other kind of input type strategy.
+User-defined functions with a single `eval()` method usually qualify for named arguments.
+
+Named arguments can be used as shown below:
+
+{{< tabs "902fe991-5fb9-4b17-ae99-f05cbd48b4dd" >}}
+{{< tab "SQL" >}}
+```text
+SELECT MyUdf(input => my_column, threshold => 42)
+```
+{{< /tab >}}
+{{< tab "Table API" >}}
+```java
+table.select(
+  call(
+    MyUdf.class,
+    $("my_column").asArgument("input"),
+    lit(42).asArgument("threshold")
+  )
+);
+```
+{{< /tab >}}
+{{< /tabs >}}
+
+{{< top >}}

[FLINK-36330][table] Session Window TVFs with named parameters don't support column expansion

Adds column expansion for Session Windows in FlinkCalciteSqlValidator.
improved_commit_message: Refactor FlinkCalciteSqlValidator to streamline table operand handling for window TVFs.
change_summary: This commit updates FlinkCalciteSqlValidator to consolidate the handling of explicit table operands into a single method, getTableOperands. This change simplifies the logic for managing both explicit tables and set semantics tables. It also adds additional test cases to verify support for the new SESSION window table function syntax and named arguments.
hints: Renamed getExplicitTableOperands to getTableOperands to reflect broader functionality.
Modified internal logic to check for both EXPLICIT_TABLE and SET_SEMANTICS_TABLE within operator methods.
Updated operand handling for various SqlKind checks to accommodate new syntax cases for window functions.
Introduced new test cases to ensure appropriate column resolution for SESSION windows using both traditional and modern syntax.

orig_commit_message:
Revert "[FLINK-33668][runtime] Redefine the redistribution logic of the NetworkBufferPool"

This reverts commit 012b8936e119d1bfadadee3182cf86d25c6dd019.
improved_commit_message: Refactor BufferPool interfaces to improve clarity and consistency
change_summary: This commit replaces instances of expected and minimum memory segment methods with a unified 'getNumberOfRequiredMemorySegments' method across BufferPool interfaces and implementations. It aims to simplify the API and enhance clarity by ensuring consistency in how buffer segment requirements are represented.
hints: Renamed 'getExpectedNumberOfMemorySegments' to 'getNumberOfRequiredMemorySegments' for clarity.
Updated BufferPool interface methods to reflect new naming convention.
Modified all implementing classes to replace old method calls with the new method.
Made minor adjustments in the documentation to reflect the changes in the API.

improved_commit_message: Refactor hint handling from join hints to query hints in the Flink SQL planner.
change_summary: This commit updates the handling of hints within the Flink SQL query planning. The previous logic that focused on join hints has been generalized to handle query hints, including join and state TTL hints. This change aims to improve the flexibility and maintainability of hint processing, allowing for clearer hint propagation and capitalization logic.
hints: Renamed classes and methods from related to join hints to query hints.
Updated hint propagation logic to account for both join and state TTL hints.
Introduced new utility methods to deal with query hints effectively.
Modified tests to validate the new query hint mechanism.

[FLINK-37632][table] Add changelog support to PTFs

This closes #26527.
improved_commit_message: Add support for updating tables and changelog modes in PTFs
change_summary: This commit introduces the ability for Process Table Functions (PTFs) to handle updating tables, implement changelog semantics, and provide enhanced functionality for data processing pipelines. The refactoring allows the PTFs to manage different changelog modes such as upsert and retract, enabling them to generate outputs that are consistent with the type of input table operations.
hints: Extended PTFs to support updating tables through static argument traits.
Implemented changelog modes to define how updates and deletions are processed and emitted.
Refactored the internal processes of PTFs to handle RowKind changes and maintain a clear semantic structure.
Added tests to ensure correct behavior when handling updates, especially regarding partition keys and upsert behaviors.

+Updates and Changelogs
+----------------------
+
+By default, PTFs assume that table arguments are backed by append-only tables, where new records are inserted to the table
+without any updates to existing records. PTFs then produce new append-only tables as output.
+
+While append-only tables are ideal and work seamlessly with event-time and watermarks, there are scenarios that require
+working with updating tables. In these cases, records can be updated or deleted after their initial insertion.
+This impacts several aspects:
+
+- **State Management**: Operations must accommodate the possibility that any record can be updated again, potentially requiring
+  a larger state footprint.
+- **Pipeline Complexity**: Since records are not final and can be changed subsequently, the entire pipeline result remains
+  in-flight.
+- **Downstream Systems**: In-flight data can lead to issues, not only in Flink but also in downstream systems where consistency
+  and finality of data are critical.
+
+{{< hint info >}}
+For efficient and high-performance data processing, it is recommended to design pipelines using append-only tables whenever
+feasible to simplify state management and avoid complexities associated with updating tables.
+{{< /hint >}}
+
+A PTF can consume and/or produce updating tables if it is configured to do so. This section provides a brief overview of
+CDC (Change Data Capture) with PTFs.
+
+### Change Data Capture Basics
+
+Under the hood, tables in Flink's SQL engine are backed by changelogs. These changelogs encode CDC (Change Data Capture)
+information containing *INSERT* (`+I`), *UPDATE_BEFORE* (`-U`), *UPDATE_AFTER* (`+U`), or *DELETE* (`-D`) messages.
+
+The existence of these flags in the changelog constitutes the *Changelog Mode* of a consumer or producer:
+
+**Append Mode `{+I}`**
+- All messages are insert-only.
+- Every insertion message is an immutable fact.
+- Messages can be distributed in an arbitrary fashion across partitions and processors because they are unrelated.
+
+**Upsert Mode `{+I, +U, -D}`**
+- Messages can contain updates leading to an updating table.
+- Updates are related using a key (i.e. the *upsert key*).
+- Every message is either an upsert or delete message for a result under the upsert key.
+- Messages for the same upsert key should land at the same partition and processor.
+- Deletions can contain only values for upsert key columns (i.e. *partial deletes*) or values for
+  all columns (i.e. *full deletes*).
+- The mode is also known as *partial image* in the literature because `-U` messages are missing.
+
+**Retract Mode `{+I, -U, +U, -D}`**
+- Messages can contain updates leading to an updating table.
+- Every insertion or update event is a fact that can be "undone" (i.e. retracted).
+- Updates are related by all columns. In simplified words: The entire row is kind of the key but duplicates are supported.
+  For example: `+I['Bob', 42]` is related to `-D['Bob', 42]` and `+U['Alice', 13]` is related to `-U['Alice', 13]`.
+- Thus, every message is either an insertion (`+`) or its retraction (`-`).
+- The mode is known as *full image* in the literature.
+
+### Updating Input Tables
+
+The `ArgumentTrait.SUPPORTS_UPDATES` instructs the system that updates are allowed as input to the given table argument.
+By default, a table argument is insert-only and updates will be rejected.
+
+Input tables become updating when sub queries such as aggregations or outer joins force an incremental computation. For
+example, the following query only works if the function is able to digest retraction messages:
+
+```text
+// The change +I[1] followed by -U[1], +U[2], -U[2], +U[3] will enter the function
+// if `table_arg` is declared with SUPPORTS_UPDATES
+WITH UpdatingTable AS (
+  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (VALUES 1, 2, 3)
+)
+SELECT * FROM f(table_arg => TABLE UpdatingTable)
+```
+
+If updates should be supported, ensure that the data type of the table argument is chosen in a way that it can encode
+changes. In other words: choose a `Row` type that exposes the `RowKind` change flag.
+
+The changelog of the backing input table decides which kinds of changes enter the function. The function receives `{+I}`
+when the input table is append-only. The function receives `{+I,+U,-D}` if the input table is upserting using the same
+upsert key as the partition key. Otherwise, retractions `{+I,-U,+U,-D}` (i.e. including `RowKind.UPDATE_BEFORE`) enter
+the function. Use `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE` to enforce retractions for all updating cases.
+
+For upserting tables, if the changelog contains key-only deletions (also known as partial deletions), only upsert key
+fields are set when a row enters the function. Non-key fields are set to `null`, regardless of `NOT NULL` constraints.
+Use `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_FULL_DELETE` to enforce that only full deletes enter the function.
+
+The `SUPPORTS_UPDATES` trait is intended for advanced use cases. Please note that inputs are always insert-only in batch
+mode. Thus, if the PTF should produce the same results in both batch and streaming mode, results should be emitted based
+on watermarks and event-time.
+
+#### Enforcing Retract Mode
+
+The `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE` instructs the system that a table argument which `SUPPORT_UPDATES` should include
+a `RowKind.UPDATE_BEFORE` message when encoding updates. In other words: it enforces presenting the updating table in
+retract changelog mode.
+
+By default, updates are encoded as emitted by the input operation. Thus, the updating table might be encoded in upsert
+changelog mode and deletes might only contain keys.
+
+The following example shows how the input changelog encodes updates differently:
+
+```text
+// Given a table UpdatingTable(name STRING PRIMARY KEY, score INT)
+// backed by upsert changelog with changes
+// +I[Alice, 42], +I[Bob, 0], +U[Bob, 2], +U[Bob, 100], -D[Bob, NULL].
+
+// Given a function `f` that declares `table_arg` with REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE.
+SELECT * FROM f(table_arg => TABLE UpdatingTable PARTITION BY name)
+
+// The following changes will enter the function:
+// +I[Alice, 42], +I[Bob, 0], -U[Bob, 0], +U[Bob, 2], -U[Bob, 2], +U[Bob, 100], -U[Bob, 100]
+
+// In both encodings, a materialized table would only contain a row for Alice.
+```
+
+#### Enforcing Upserts with Full Deletes
+
+The `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_FULL_DELETE` instructs the system that a table argument which `SUPPORT_UPDATES` should include
+all fields in the `RowKind.DELETE` message if the updating table is backed by an upsert changelog.
+
+For upserting tables, if the changelog contains key-only deletes (also known as partial deletes), only upsert key fields
+are set when a row enters the function. Non-key fields are set to null, regardless of NOT NULL constraints.
+
+The following example shows how the input changelog encodes updates differently:
+
+```text
+// Given a table UpdatingTable(name STRING PRIMARY KEY, score INT)
+// backed by upsert changelog with changes
+// +I[Alice, 42], +I[Bob, 0], +U[Bob, 2], +U[Bob, 100], -D[Bob, NULL].
+
+// Given a function `f` that declares `table_arg` with REQUIRE_FULL_DELETE.
+SELECT * FROM f(table_arg => TABLE UpdatingTable PARTITION BY name)
+
+// The following changes will enter the function:
+// +I[Alice, 42], +I[Bob, 0], +U[Bob, 2], +U[Bob, 100], -D[Bob, 100].
+
+// In both encodings, a materialized table would only contain a row for Alice.
+```
+
+#### Example: Changelog Filtering
+
+The following function demonstrates how a PTF can transform an updating table into an append-only table. Instead of
+applying updates encoded in each `Row`, it incorporates the changelog flag into the payload. The rows emitted by the PTF
+are guaranteed to be of `RowKind.INSERT`. By preserving the original changelog flag in the payload, it permits filtering
+of specific update types. In this example, it filters out all deletions.
+
+{{< tabs "1937eeed-3d13-455c-8e2f-5e164da9f844" >}}
+{{< tab "Java" >}}
+```java
+TableEnvironment env = TableEnvironment.create(EnvironmentSettings.inStreamingMode());
+
+Table data = env
+  .fromValues(
+    Row.of("Bob", 23),
+    Row.of("Alice", 42),
+    Row.of("Alice", 2))
+  .as("name", "score");
+
+// Since the aggregation is not windowed and potentially unbounded,
+// the result is an updating table. Usually, this means that all following
+// operations and sinks need to support updates.
+Table aggregated = data
+  .groupBy($("name"))
+  .select($("name"), $("score").sum().as("sum"));
+
+// However, the PTF will convert the updating table into an insert-only result.
+// Subsequent operations and sinks can easily digest the resulting table.
+Table changelog = aggregated
+  .partitionBy($("name"))
+  .process(ToChangelogFunction.class);
+
+// For event-driven applications, filtering on certain CDC events is possible.
+Table upsertsOnly = changelog.filter($("flag").in("INSERT", "UPDATE_AFTER"));
+
+upsertsOnly.execute().print();
+
+// --------------------
+// Function declaration
+// --------------------
+
+@DataTypeHint("ROW<flag STRING, sum INT>")
+public static class ToChangelogFunction extends ProcessTableFunction<Row> {
+  public void eval(@ArgumentHint({TABLE_AS_SET, SUPPORT_UPDATES}) Row input) {
+    // Forwards the sum column and includes the row's kind as a string column.
+    Row changelogRow =
+      Row.of(
+        input.getKind().toString(),
+        input.getField("sum"));
+
+    collect(changelogRow);
+  }
+}
+```
+{{< /tab >}}
+{{< /tabs >}}
+
+The PTF produces the following output when debugging in a console. The `op` section indicates that the result is append-only. The
+original flag is encoded in the `flag` column.
+
+```text
++----+--------------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------+
+| op |                           name |                           flag |         sum |
++----+--------------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------+
+| +I |                            Bob |                         INSERT |          23 |
+| +I |                          Alice |                         INSERT |          42 |
+| +I |                          Alice |                   UPDATE_AFTER |          44 |
++----+--------------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------+
+```
+
+#### Limitations
+- The `ArgumentTrait.PASS_COLUMNS_THROUGH` is not supported if `ArgumentTrait.SUPPORTS_UPDATES` is declared.
+- The `on_time` argument is not supported if the PTF receives updates.
+
+### Updating Function Output
+
+The `ChangelogFunction` interface makes it possible for a function to declare the types of changes (e.g., inserts, updates,
+deletes) that it may emit, allowing the planner to make informed decisions during query planning.
+
+{{< hint info >}}
+The interface is intended for advanced use cases and should be implemented with care. Emitting an incorrect changelog
+from the PTF may lead to undefined behavior in the overall query.
+{{< /hint >}}
+
+The resulting changelog mode can be influenced by:
+- The changelog mode of the input table arguments, accessible via `ChangelogContext.getTableChangelogMode(int)`.
+- The changelog mode required by downstream operators, accessible via `ChangelogContext.getRequiredChangelogMode()`.
+
+Changelog mode inference in the planner involves several steps. The `getChangelogMode(ChangelogContext)` method is
+called for each step:
+
+1. The planner checks whether the PTF emits updates or inserts-only.
+2. If updates are emitted, the planner determines whether the updates include {@link
+   RowKind#UPDATE_BEFORE} messages (retract mode), or whether {@link RowKind#UPDATE_AFTER}
+   messages are sufficient (upsert mode). For this, {@link #getChangelogMode} might be called
+   twice to query both retract mode and upsert mode capabilities as indicated by {@link
+   ChangelogContext#getRequiredChangelogMode()}.
+3. If in upsert mode, the planner checks whether {@link RowKind#DELETE} messages contain all
+   fields (full deletes) or only key fields (partial deletes). In the case of partial deletes,
+   only the upsert key fields are set when a row is removed; all non-key fields are null,
+   regardless of nullability constraints. {@link ChangelogContext#getRequiredChangelogMode()}
+   indicates whether a downstream operator requires full deletes.
+
+Emitting changelogs is only valid for PTFs that take table arguments with set semantics (see `ArgumentTrait.TABLE_AS_SET`).
+In case of upserts, the upsert key must be equal to the PARTITION BY key.
+
+It is perfectly valid for a `ChangelogFunction` implementation to return a fixed `ChangelogMode`, regardless of the
+`ChangelogContext`. This approach may be appropriate when the PTF is designed for a specific scenario or pipeline setup,
+and does not need to adapt dynamically to different input modes. Note that in such cases, the PTFs applicability is limited,
+as it may only function correctly within the predefined context for which it was designed.
+
+In some cases, this interface should be used in combination with `SpecializedFunction`
+to reconfigure the PTF after the final changelog mode for the specific call location has been
+determined. The final changelog mode is also available during runtime via
+`ProcessTableFunction.Context.getChangelogMode()`.
+
+#### Example: Custom Aggregation
+
+The following function demonstrates how a PTF can implement an aggregation function that is able to emit updates based
+on custom conditional logic. The function takes a table of score results partitioned by `name` and maintains a sum per
+partition. Scores that are lower than `0` are treated as incorrect and invalidate the entire aggregation for this key.
+
+{{< tabs "2037eeed-3d13-455c-8e2f-5e164da9f844" >}}
+{{< tab "Java" >}}
+```java
+TableEnvironment env = TableEnvironment.create(EnvironmentSettings.inStreamingMode());
+
+Table data = env
+  .fromValues(
+    Row.of("Bob", 23),
+    Row.of("Alice", 42),
+    Row.of("Alice", 2),
+    Row.of("Bob", -1),
+    Row.of("Bob", 45))
+  .as("name", "score");
+
+// Call the PTF on an append-only table
+Table aggregated = data
+  .partitionBy($("name"))
+  .process(CustomAggregation.class);
+
+aggregated.execute().print();
+
+// --------------------
+// Function declaration
+// --------------------
+
+@DataTypeHint("ROW<sum INT>")
+public static class CustomAggregation
+  extends ProcessTableFunction<Row>
+  implements ChangelogFunction {
+
+  @Override
+  public ChangelogMode getChangelogMode(ChangelogContext changelogContext) {
+    // Tells the system that the PTF produces updates encoded as retractions
+    return ChangelogMode.all();
+  }
+
+  public static class Accumulator {
+    public Integer sum = 0;
+  }
+
+  public void eval(@StateHint Accumulator state, @ArgumentHint(TABLE_AS_SET) Row input) {
+    int score = input.getFieldAs("score");
+
+    // A negative state indicates that the partition
+    // key has been marked as invalid before
+    if (state.sum == -1) {
+      return;
+    }
+
+    // A negative score marks the entire aggregation result as invalid.
+    if (score < 0) {
+      // Send out a -D for the affected partition key and
+      // mark the invalidation in state. All subsequent operations
+      // and sinks will remove the aggregation result.
+      collect(Row.ofKind(RowKind.DELETE, state.sum));
+      state.sum = -1;
+    } else {
+      if (state.sum == 0) {
+        // Emit +I for the first valid aggregation result.
+        state.sum += score;
+        collect(Row.ofKind(RowKind.INSERT, state.sum));
+      } else {
+        // Emit -U (with old aggregation result) and +U (with new aggregation result)
+        // for encoding the update.
+        collect(Row.ofKind(RowKind.UPDATE_BEFORE, state.sum));
+        state.sum += score;
+        collect(Row.ofKind(RowKind.UPDATE_AFTER, state.sum));
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+{{< /tab >}}
+{{< /tabs >}}
+
+The PTF produces the following output when debugging in a console. The `op` section indicates that the result is updating. However,
+no updates to `Bob` are forwarded after the invalid `-1` is received, causing the PTF to ignore the update with value `45`.
+The aggregation results for `Alice` contain only valid scores and are preserved in a materialized table.
+
+```text
++----+--------------------------------+-------------+
+| op |                           name |         sum |
++----+--------------------------------+-------------+
+| +I |                            Bob |          23 |
+| +I |                          Alice |          42 |
+| -U |                          Alice |          42 |
+| +U |                          Alice |          44 |
+| -D |                            Bob |          23 |
++----+--------------------------------+-------------+
+```
+
+#### Limitations
+- The `on_time` argument is not supported if the PTF emits updates.
+- Currently, it is difficult to test upsert PTFs because debugging sinks such as `collect()` operate in retract mode and
+  will request retract support from any PTF. Upserting PTFs have to be tested with upserting sinks (e.g. `kafka-upsert` connector).
+
+{{< top >}}
+

+The `ArgumentTrait.SUPPORTS_UPDATES` instructs the system that updates are allowed as input to the given table argument.

+// The change +I[1] followed by -U[1], +U[2], -U[2], +U[3] will enter the function
+// if `table_arg` is declared with SUPPORTS_UPDATES

+  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (VALUES 1, 2, 3)

+changes. In other words: choose a `Row` type that exposes the `RowKind` change flag.

+when the input table is append-only. The function receives `{+I,+U,-D}` if the input table is upserting using the same

+the function. Use `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE` to enforce retractions for all updating cases.

+mode. Thus, if the PTF should produce the same results in both batch and streaming mode, results should be emitted based

+#### Enforcing Retract Mode

+The `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE` instructs the system that a table argument which `SUPPORT_UPDATES` should include

+of specific update types. In this example, it filters out all deletions.

+TableEnvironment env = TableEnvironment.create(EnvironmentSettings.inStreamingMode());

+Table data = env

+// Function declaration
+// --------------------

+  public void eval(@ArgumentHint({TABLE_AS_SET, SUPPORT_UPDATES}) Row input) {

+called for each step:

+The following function demonstrates how a PTF can implement an aggregation function that is able to emit updates based
+on custom conditional logic. The function takes a table of score results partitioned by `name` and maintains a sum per
+partition. Scores that are lower than `0` are treated as incorrect and invalidate the entire aggregation for this key.

+{{< tabs "2037eeed-3d13-455c-8e2f-5e164da9f844" >}}
+{{< tab "Java" >}}
+```java
+TableEnvironment env = TableEnvironment.create(EnvironmentSettings.inStreamingMode());
+
+Table data = env
+  .fromValues(
+    Row.of("Bob", 23),
+    Row.of("Alice", 42),
+    Row.of("Alice", 2),
+    Row.of("Bob", -1),
+    Row.of("Bob", 45))
+  .as("name", "score");
+
+// Call the PTF on an append-only table
+Table aggregated = data
+  .partitionBy($("name"))
+  .process(CustomAggregation.class);
+
+aggregated.execute().print();

+// --------------------
+// Function declaration
+// --------------------
+
+@DataTypeHint("ROW<sum INT>")
+public static class CustomAggregation
+  extends ProcessTableFunction<Row>
+  implements ChangelogFunction {
+
+  @Override
+  public ChangelogMode getChangelogMode(ChangelogContext changelogContext) {
+    // Tells the system that the PTF produces updates encoded as retractions
+    return ChangelogMode.all();
+  }
+
+  public static class Accumulator {
+    public Integer sum = 0;
+  }
+
+  public void eval(@StateHint Accumulator state, @ArgumentHint(TABLE_AS_SET) Row input) {
+    int score = input.getFieldAs("score");
+
+    // A negative state indicates that the partition
+    // key has been marked as invalid before
+    if (state.sum == -1) {
+      return;
+    }
+
+    // A negative score marks the entire aggregation result as invalid.
+    if (score < 0) {
+      // Send out a -D for the affected partition key and
+      // mark the invalidation in state. All subsequent operations
+      // and sinks will remove the aggregation result.
+      collect(Row.ofKind(RowKind.DELETE, state.sum));
+      state.sum = -1;
+    } else {
+      if (state.sum == 0) {
+        // Emit +I for the first valid aggregation result.
+        state.sum += score;
+        collect(Row.ofKind(RowKind.INSERT, state.sum));
+      } else {
+        // Emit -U (with old aggregation result) and +U (with new aggregation result)
+        // for encoding the update.
+        collect(Row.ofKind(RowKind.UPDATE_BEFORE, state.sum));
+        state.sum += score;
+        collect(Row.ofKind(RowKind.UPDATE_AFTER, state.sum));
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+{{< /tab >}}
+{{< /tabs >}}

+The PTF produces the following output when debugging in a console. The `op` section indicates that the result is updating. However,
+no updates to `Bob` are forwarded after the invalid `-1` is received, causing the PTF to ignore the update with value `45`.
+The aggregation results for `Alice` contain only valid scores and are preserved in a materialized table.

+```text
++----+--------------------------------+-------------+
+| op |                           name |         sum |
++----+--------------------------------+-------------+
+| +I |                            Bob |          23 |
+| +I |                          Alice |          42 |
+| -U |                          Alice |          42 |
+| +U |                          Alice |          44 |
+| -D |                            Bob |          23 |
++----+--------------------------------+-------------+
+```

+- The `on_time` argument is not supported if the PTF emits updates.

+  will request retract support from any PTF. Upserting PTFs have to be tested with upserting sinks (e.g. `kafka-upsert` connector).

+working with updating tables. In these cases, records can be updated or deleted after their initial insertion.

+  a larger state footprint.
+- **Pipeline Complexity**: Since records are not final and can be changed subsequently, the entire pipeline result remains
+  in-flight.
+- **Downstream Systems**: In-flight data can lead to issues, not only in Flink but also in downstream systems where consistency
+  and finality of data are critical.
+

+For efficient and high-performance data processing, it is recommended to design pipelines using append-only tables whenever
+feasible to simplify state management and avoid complexities associated with updating tables.

+The existence of these flags in the changelog constitutes the *Changelog Mode* of a consumer or producer:

+**Append Mode `{+I}`**
+- All messages are insert-only.
+- Every insertion message is an immutable fact.
+- Messages can be distributed in an arbitrary fashion across partitions and processors because they are unrelated.

+- Messages can contain updates leading to an updating table.
+- Updates are related using a key (i.e. the *upsert key*).

+- Messages for the same upsert key should land at the same partition and processor.

+  all columns (i.e. *full deletes*).

+{{< tab "Java" >}}
+```java
+TableEnvironment env = TableEnvironment.create(EnvironmentSettings.inStreamingMode());
+
+Table data = env
+  .fromValues(
+    Row.of("Bob", 23),
+    Row.of("Alice", 42),

+    Row.of("Bob", 45))

+// Function declaration

+@DataTypeHint("ROW<sum INT>")
+public static class CustomAggregation
+  extends ProcessTableFunction<Row>
+  implements ChangelogFunction {

+  @Override
+  public ChangelogMode getChangelogMode(ChangelogContext changelogContext) {
+    // Tells the system that the PTF produces updates encoded as retractions
+    return ChangelogMode.all();
+  }
+
+  public static class Accumulator {
+    public Integer sum = 0;
+  }
+
+  public void eval(@StateHint Accumulator state, @ArgumentHint(TABLE_AS_SET) Row input) {
+    int score = input.getFieldAs("score");
+

+    if (state.sum == -1) {

+      // and sinks will remove the aggregation result.

+      state.sum = -1;

+        // for encoding the update.

+      }

+Updates and Changelogs
+----------------------
+
+By default, PTFs assume that table arguments are backed by append-only tables, where new records are inserted to the table
+without any updates to existing records. PTFs then produce new append-only tables as output.
+
+While append-only tables are ideal and work seamlessly with event-time and watermarks, there are scenarios that require
+working with updating tables. In these cases, records can be updated or deleted after their initial insertion.
+This impacts several aspects:
+
+- **State Management**: Operations must accommodate the possibility that any record can be updated again, potentially requiring
+  a larger state footprint.
+- **Pipeline Complexity**: Since records are not final and can be changed subsequently, the entire pipeline result remains
+  in-flight.
+- **Downstream Systems**: In-flight data can lead to issues, not only in Flink but also in downstream systems where consistency
+  and finality of data are critical.
+
+{{< hint info >}}
+For efficient and high-performance data processing, it is recommended to design pipelines using append-only tables whenever
+feasible to simplify state management and avoid complexities associated with updating tables.
+{{< /hint >}}
+
+A PTF can consume and/or produce updating tables if it is configured to do so. This section provides a brief overview of
+CDC (Change Data Capture) with PTFs.
+
+### Change Data Capture Basics
+
+Under the hood, tables in Flink's SQL engine are backed by changelogs. These changelogs encode CDC (Change Data Capture)
+information containing *INSERT* (`+I`), *UPDATE_BEFORE* (`-U`), *UPDATE_AFTER* (`+U`), or *DELETE* (`-D`) messages.
+
+The existence of these flags in the changelog constitutes the *Changelog Mode* of a consumer or producer:
+
+**Append Mode `{+I}`**
+- All messages are insert-only.
+- Every insertion message is an immutable fact.
+- Messages can be distributed in an arbitrary fashion across partitions and processors because they are unrelated.
+
+**Upsert Mode `{+I, +U, -D}`**
+- Messages can contain updates leading to an updating table.
+- Updates are related using a key (i.e. the *upsert key*).
+- Every message is either an upsert or delete message for a result under the upsert key.
+- Messages for the same upsert key should land at the same partition and processor.
+- Deletions can contain only values for upsert key columns (i.e. *partial deletes*) or values for
+  all columns (i.e. *full deletes*).
+- The mode is also known as *partial image* in the literature because `-U` messages are missing.
+
+**Retract Mode `{+I, -U, +U, -D}`**
+- Messages can contain updates leading to an updating table.
+- Every insertion or update event is a fact that can be "undone" (i.e. retracted).
+- Updates are related by all columns. In simplified words: The entire row is kind of the key but duplicates are supported.
+  For example: `+I['Bob', 42]` is related to `-D['Bob', 42]` and `+U['Alice', 13]` is related to `-U['Alice', 13]`.
+- Thus, every message is either an insertion (`+`) or its retraction (`-`).
+- The mode is known as *full image* in the literature.
+
+### Updating Input Tables
+
+The `ArgumentTrait.SUPPORTS_UPDATES` instructs the system that updates are allowed as input to the given table argument.
+By default, a table argument is insert-only and updates will be rejected.
+
+Input tables become updating when sub queries such as aggregations or outer joins force an incremental computation. For
+example, the following query only works if the function is able to digest retraction messages:
+
+```text
+// The change +I[1] followed by -U[1], +U[2], -U[2], +U[3] will enter the function
+// if `table_arg` is declared with SUPPORTS_UPDATES
+WITH UpdatingTable AS (
+  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (VALUES 1, 2, 3)
+)
+SELECT * FROM f(table_arg => TABLE UpdatingTable)
+```
+
+If updates should be supported, ensure that the data type of the table argument is chosen in a way that it can encode
+changes. In other words: choose a `Row` type that exposes the `RowKind` change flag.
+
+The changelog of the backing input table decides which kinds of changes enter the function. The function receives `{+I}`
+when the input table is append-only. The function receives `{+I,+U,-D}` if the input table is upserting using the same
+upsert key as the partition key. Otherwise, retractions `{+I,-U,+U,-D}` (i.e. including `RowKind.UPDATE_BEFORE`) enter
+the function. Use `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE` to enforce retractions for all updating cases.
+
+For upserting tables, if the changelog contains key-only deletions (also known as partial deletions), only upsert key
+fields are set when a row enters the function. Non-key fields are set to `null`, regardless of `NOT NULL` constraints.
+Use `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_FULL_DELETE` to enforce that only full deletes enter the function.
+
+The `SUPPORTS_UPDATES` trait is intended for advanced use cases. Please note that inputs are always insert-only in batch
+mode. Thus, if the PTF should produce the same results in both batch and streaming mode, results should be emitted based
+on watermarks and event-time.
+
+#### Enforcing Retract Mode
+
+The `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE` instructs the system that a table argument which `SUPPORT_UPDATES` should include
+a `RowKind.UPDATE_BEFORE` message when encoding updates. In other words: it enforces presenting the updating table in
+retract changelog mode.
+
+By default, updates are encoded as emitted by the input operation. Thus, the updating table might be encoded in upsert
+changelog mode and deletes might only contain keys.
+
+The following example shows how the input changelog encodes updates differently:
+
+```text
+// Given a table UpdatingTable(name STRING PRIMARY KEY, score INT)
+// backed by upsert changelog with changes
+// +I[Alice, 42], +I[Bob, 0], +U[Bob, 2], +U[Bob, 100], -D[Bob, NULL].
+
+// Given a function `f` that declares `table_arg` with REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE.
+SELECT * FROM f(table_arg => TABLE UpdatingTable PARTITION BY name)
+
+// The following changes will enter the function:
+// +I[Alice, 42], +I[Bob, 0], -U[Bob, 0], +U[Bob, 2], -U[Bob, 2], +U[Bob, 100], -U[Bob, 100]
+
+// In both encodings, a materialized table would only contain a row for Alice.
+```
+
+#### Enforcing Upserts with Full Deletes
+
+The `ArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_FULL_DELETE` instructs the system that a table argument which `SUPPORT_UPDATES` should include
+all fields in the `RowKind.DELETE` message if the updating table is backed by an upsert changelog.
+
+For upserting tables, if the changelog contains key-only deletes (also known as partial deletes), only upsert key fields
+are set when a row enters the function. Non-key fields are set to null, regardless of NOT NULL constraints.
+
+The following example shows how the input changelog encodes updates differently:
+
+```text
+// Given a table UpdatingTable(name STRING PRIMARY KEY, score INT)
+// backed by upsert changelog with changes
+// +I[Alice, 42], +I[Bob, 0], +U[Bob, 2], +U[Bob, 100], -D[Bob, NULL].
+
+// Given a function `f` that declares `table_arg` with REQUIRE_FULL_DELETE.
+SELECT * FROM f(table_arg => TABLE UpdatingTable PARTITION BY name)
+
+// The following changes will enter the function:
+// +I[Alice, 42], +I[Bob, 0], +U[Bob, 2], +U[Bob, 100], -D[Bob, 100].
+
+// In both encodings, a materialized table would only contain a row for Alice.
+```
+
+#### Example: Changelog Filtering
+
+The following function demonstrates how a PTF can transform an updating table into an append-only table. Instead of
+applying updates encoded in each `Row`, it incorporates the changelog flag into the payload. The rows emitted by the PTF
+are guaranteed to be of `RowKind.INSERT`. By preserving the original changelog flag in the payload, it permits filtering
+of specific update types. In this example, it filters out all deletions.
+
+{{< tabs "1937eeed-3d13-455c-8e2f-5e164da9f844" >}}
+{{< tab "Java" >}}
+```java
+TableEnvironment env = TableEnvironment.create(EnvironmentSettings.inStreamingMode());
+
+Table data = env
+  .fromValues(
+    Row.of("Bob", 23),
+    Row.of("Alice", 42),
+    Row.of("Alice", 2))
+  .as("name", "score");
+
+// Since the aggregation is not windowed and potentially unbounded,
+// the result is an updating table. Usually, this means that all following
+// operations and sinks need to support updates.
+Table aggregated = data
+  .groupBy($("name"))
+  .select($("name"), $("score").sum().as("sum"));
+
+// However, the PTF will convert the updating table into an insert-only result.
+// Subsequent operations and sinks can easily digest the resulting table.
+Table changelog = aggregated
+  .partitionBy($("name"))
+  .process(ToChangelogFunction.class);
+
+// For event-driven applications, filtering on certain CDC events is possible.
+Table upsertsOnly = changelog.filter($("flag").in("INSERT", "UPDATE_AFTER"));
+
+upsertsOnly.execute().print();
+
+// --------------------
+// Function declaration
+// --------------------
+
+@DataTypeHint("ROW<flag STRING, sum INT>")
+public static class ToChangelogFunction extends ProcessTableFunction<Row> {
+  public void eval(@ArgumentHint({TABLE_AS_SET, SUPPORT_UPDATES}) Row input) {
+    // Forwards the sum column and includes the row's kind as a string column.
+    Row changelogRow =
+      Row.of(
+        input.getKind().toString(),
+        input.getField("sum"));
+
+    collect(changelogRow);
+  }
+}
+```
+{{< /tab >}}
+{{< /tabs >}}
+
+The PTF produces the following output when debugging in a console. The `op` section indicates that the result is append-only. The
+original flag is encoded in the `flag` column.
+
+```text
++----+--------------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------+
+| op |                           name |                           flag |         sum |
++----+--------------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------+
+| +I |                            Bob |                         INSERT |          23 |
+| +I |                          Alice |                         INSERT |          42 |
+| +I |                          Alice |                   UPDATE_AFTER |          44 |
++----+--------------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------+
+```
+
+#### Limitations
+- The `ArgumentTrait.PASS_COLUMNS_THROUGH` is not supported if `ArgumentTrait.SUPPORTS_UPDATES` is declared.
+- The `on_time` argument is not supported if the PTF receives updates.

+### Updating Function Output
+
+The `ChangelogFunction` interface makes it possible for a function to declare the types of changes (e.g., inserts, updates,
+deletes) that it may emit, allowing the planner to make informed decisions during query planning.
+
+{{< hint info >}}
+The interface is intended for advanced use cases and should be implemented with care. Emitting an incorrect changelog
+from the PTF may lead to undefined behavior in the overall query.
+{{< /hint >}}
+
+The resulting changelog mode can be influenced by:
+- The changelog mode of the input table arguments, accessible via `ChangelogContext.getTableChangelogMode(int)`.
+- The changelog mode required by downstream operators, accessible via `ChangelogContext.getRequiredChangelogMode()`.
+
+Changelog mode inference in the planner involves several steps. The `getChangelogMode(ChangelogContext)` method is
+called for each step:
+
+1. The planner checks whether the PTF emits updates or inserts-only.
+2. If updates are emitted, the planner determines whether the updates include {@link
+   RowKind#UPDATE_BEFORE} messages (retract mode), or whether {@link RowKind#UPDATE_AFTER}
+   messages are sufficient (upsert mode). For this, {@link #getChangelogMode} might be called
+   twice to query both retract mode and upsert mode capabilities as indicated by {@link
+   ChangelogContext#getRequiredChangelogMode()}.
+3. If in upsert mode, the planner checks whether {@link RowKind#DELETE} messages contain all
+   fields (full deletes) or only key fields (partial deletes). In the case of partial deletes,
+   only the upsert key fields are set when a row is removed; all non-key fields are null,
+   regardless of nullability constraints. {@link ChangelogContext#getRequiredChangelogMode()}
+   indicates whether a downstream operator requires full deletes.
+
+Emitting changelogs is only valid for PTFs that take table arguments with set semantics (see `ArgumentTrait.TABLE_AS_SET`).
+In case of upserts, the upsert key must be equal to the PARTITION BY key.
+
+It is perfectly valid for a `ChangelogFunction` implementation to return a fixed `ChangelogMode`, regardless of the
+`ChangelogContext`. This approach may be appropriate when the PTF is designed for a specific scenario or pipeline setup,
+and does not need to adapt dynamically to different input modes. Note that in such cases, the PTFs applicability is limited,
+as it may only function correctly within the predefined context for which it was designed.
+
+In some cases, this interface should be used in combination with `SpecializedFunction`
+to reconfigure the PTF after the final changelog mode for the specific call location has been
+determined. The final changelog mode is also available during runtime via
+`ProcessTableFunction.Context.getChangelogMode()`.

+  private def toChangelogMode(

+  private def isPtfUpsert(

+    val fmq = FlinkRelMetadataQuery.reuseOrCreate(input.getCluster.getMetadataQuery)
+    val upsertKeys = fmq.getUpsertKeys(input)
+    if (
+      upsertKeys == null || partitionKeys.isEmpty || !upsertKeys.contains(partitionKeys)
+      || tableArg.is(StaticArgumentTrait.REQUIRE_UPDATE_BEFORE)
+    ) {

+    } else {

+    val call = process.getCall
+    val tableArgCall = call.operands.get(inputArg.i).asInstanceOf[RexTableArgCall]
+    val modifyKindSet = getModifyKindSet(child)
+    (tableArg, tableArgCall, modifyKindSet)

+  private def toPtfChangelogContext(

+        }

+          verifyPtfRequirementsForUpdates(call, requiredChangelogMode, changelogMode)

+    StreamPhysicalProcessTableFunction
+      .getProvidedInputArgs(call)
+      .map(_.e)
+      .foreach {

+                s"Table argument '${tableArg.getName}' of function '${call.getOperator.toString}' " +
+                s"must use set semantics.")
+          }
+      }
+  }
+
+  private def verifyPtfRequirementsForUpdates(
+      call: RexCall,
+      required: ChangelogMode,
+      returned: ChangelogMode): Unit = {
+    if (!required.keyOnlyDeletes() && returned.keyOnlyDeletes()) {
+      throw new ValidationException(
+        s"Unsupported changelog mode returned from PTF '${call.getOperator.toString}'. " +
+          s"The system requires that deletions include all fields in DELETE messages. " +
+          s"Key-only deletes are not sufficient.")
+    }
+  }

orig_commit_message: [FLINK-34558][state] Support tracking state size (#25837)
improved_commit_message: Add state size tracking support to Flink state backends
change_summary: This commit introduces metrics for tracking the size of various keyed state operations such as adding, updating, and retrieving values in different state types (ValueState, ListState, MapState, etc.). This functionality is governed by the configuration options for state size tracking, allowing for finer performance monitoring and optimization in Flink applications.
hints: Implemented new configuration options for enabling state size tracking.
Created new metrics classes for ListState, MapState, and ValueState to measure size during operations.
Modified existing state classes to integrate size tracking logic.
Introduced factory methods to wrap states with size tracking capability.
Updated test utilities to verify functionality of size tracking.

It is recommended to only use them for debugging purposes. +## State key/value size tracking + +Flink also allows to track the keyed state key/value size for standard Flink state-backends or customized state backends which extending from `AbstractStateBackend`. This feature is disabled by default. +To enable this feature you must set the `state.size-track.keyed-state-enabled` to true in the [Flink configuration]({{< ref "docs/deployment/config" >}}#state-backends-size-tracking-options). + +Once tracking keyed state key/value size is enabled, Flink will sample the state size every `N` access, in which `N` is defined by `state.size-track.sample-interval`. +This configuration has a default value of 100. A smaller value will get more accurate results but have a higher performance impact since it is sampled more frequently. + +As the type of this key/value size metrics is histogram, `state.size-track.history-size` will control the maximum number of recorded values in history, which has the default value of 128. +A larger value of this configuration will require more memory, but will provide a more accurate result. + +Warning Enabling state-size metrics may impact the performance. +It is recommended to only use them for debugging purposes. +If state.ttl is enabled, the size of the value will include the size of the TTL-related timestamp. +The value size of AggregatingState is not accounted for because AggregatingState returns a result processed by a user-defined AggregateFunction, whereas currently, only the actual stored data size in the state can be tracked. + ## REST API integration Metrics can be queried through the [Monitoring REST API]({{< ref "docs/ops/rest_api" >}}).

improved_commit_message: Refactor SinkV2 Committer and Writer Implementations
change_summary: Enhanced the SinkV2 implementation by improving the structure of the committer and writer classes. This includes introducing new serializable record handling and ensuring a better type safety during commit operations. Also, refactored several parts of the test cases to reflect changes in how records are processed in streamed and batch modes.
hints: Replaced String based committable handling with a generic Record class to improve type safety.
Modified commit methods to handle typed records instead of generic strings.
Updated tests to ensure they now interact with the new Record type, improving the clarity and correctness of test assertions.
Consolidated the use of serializers for the new Record class throughout the Sink functionalities.

change_summary: This commit refactors the representation of job plans in the Flink codebase. The JobPlanInfo class now uses a structured Plan object that separates job details into distinct fields, enhancing clarity, maintainability, and usability. This change also includes updates throughout the codebase to accommodate the new structure and ensures every reference to the JobPlanInfo reflects this new design.

Introduced nested classes for Plan and Node details to encapsulate job structure better.
Replaced all instances of jsonPlan manipulation with structured Plan interactions in the relevant methods.
Refactored tests to ensure that they validate the new structured form of the job plan.

orig_commit_message: [FLINK-37426][metrics] Properly integrate traces with metric group features
improved_commit_message: Refactor telemetry reporting and configuration system to accommodate span filtering and enhancements.
change_summary: This commit introduces significant enhancements to the telemetry reporting system, including splitting metric and span reporting configurations. The refactoring involves the introduction of a unified filtering mechanism for both metrics and traces and reorganizes the configuration options for cleaner handling of reporter settings.
hints: Created a generic ReporterFilter interface for filtering spans and metrics.
Separated the filtering logic into MetricReporterFilter and TraceReporterFilter.
Utilized a new DefaultReporterFilters class to define default filtering mechanisms from configuration.
Enhanced TraceOptions configuration to streamline reporter settings and included additional variables.
Updated tests to validate new behavior and interaction of reporters with spans and metrics.

orig_commit_message:
[FLINK-37423][table] Support PTFs in Table API

This closes #26331.
improved_commit_message: Add support for new table functions and improve process table functionality
change_summary: This commit introduces new methods for handling process table functions, including support for partitioned tables, both in SQL and Table API. It also improves the integration of user-defined functions with the framework, allowing for more flexibility in table processing.
hints: Added 'fromCall' methods to handle calls to user-defined functions in a consistent manner.
Refactored existing table function handling to streamline the processing of arguments and outputs.
Enhanced error messages for better debugging of user-defined function calls.
Implemented inline function handling to allow for inline processing in Table API.

Introduced RecoveryClaimMode to manage file ownership claims during state restoration and transfer, thus simplifying the logic of state handle management in the context of recovery and fault tolerance.

Enhanced the logic for file ownership management based on the new RecoveryClaimMode enum.
Refactored condition checks in file registration and deletion methods for clarity.
Improved test coverage around file restoration and snapshots to ensure comprehensive functionality with the new recovery strategies.

+package org.apache.flink.state.forst.fs.filemapping;
+
+/** Indicates the ownership of a file in ForSt DB. */
+public enum FileOwnership {
+    /**
+     * The file is privately owned by DB. "Owned by DB" means the file's lifecycle is managed by DB,
+     * i.e., it will be deleted when DB decides to dispose of it. "Privately" indicates that its
+     * ownership cannot be transferred to JM.
+     */
+    PRIVATE_OWNED_BY_DB,
+
+    /**
+     * The file is owned by DB but is shareable. "Shareable" means its ownership can be transferred
+     * to JM in the future.
+     */
+    SHAREABLE_OWNED_BY_DB,
+
+    /**
+     * The file is not owned by DB. That means its lifecycle is not managed by DB, and only JM can
+     * decide when to delete it.
+     */
+    NOT_OWNED
+}

hints: Replaced job graph related methods with corresponding stream graph methods.
Modified the submit job logic to work directly with StreamGraph.
Updated the notification methods to reflect changes from JobGraph to StreamGraph.
Ensured that StreamGraph is consistently used across various executors and factories.

orig_commit_message: [FLINK-36336] Remove deprecated dataset API exclude table module
improved_commit_message: Refactor code to use StreamExecutionEnvironment and improve data stream handling
change_summary: Refactored the existing code to replace ExecutionEnvironment with StreamExecutionEnvironment across various classes and methods. This enhances compatibility with the DataStream API and improves the performance of streaming jobs. Various methods for handling data input and output were updated to utilize DataStreamSources and sinks instead of DataSets.
hints: Replaced 'ExecutionEnvironment' with 'StreamExecutionEnvironment' in the test cases.
Converted DataSets to DataStreams in existing test data utilities.
Used DataStream 'map', 'join', and 'keyBy' functionalities for transformations instead of the DataSet methods.
Ensured compatibility with both old DataSet and new DataStream APIs to maintain existing test cases.
Updated method signatures and return types to support Stream API.

orig_commit_message: [FLINK-36251][streaming-java] Remove StateBackend-related configuration getters/setters that return/set complex Java objects.
improved_commit_message: Refactor state backend configuration for StreamExecutionEnvironment
change_summary: This commit refactors the way state backends are configured within the StreamExecutionEnvironment, replacing deprecated methods with new configurations using StateBackendUtils. The changes also streamline the checkpointing configuration across various test cases, enhancing the overall consistency and simplifying the process.
hints: Replaced direct calls to setStateBackend with utility methods from StateBackendUtils.
Unified checkpointing configurations using CheckpointStorageUtils.
Removed deprecated state backend methods to prevent warnings in future versions.
Consolidated hash map and RocksDB state backend setups under a single utility method for clarity.

patch.improved_commit_message: Refactor rescaling management to state transition management
patch.change_summary: This commit replaces the RescaleManager with a new StateTransitionManager for handling state transitions within AdaptiveScheduler. The change includes renaming and modifying associated classes and their usage across the codebase. This refactor improves clarity and maintainability by consolidating transition logic into a dedicated manager.
hints: Renamed RescaleManager to StateTransitionManager to better reflect its purpose.
Updated method names and interfaces to align with the new state transition logic.
All instances where RescaleManager was used have been replaced with StateTransitionManager, ensuring that functionalities can seamlessly transition.
Introduced phases (Cooldown, Idling, Stabilizing, etc.) to represent different states within the state transition process.

patch.orig_commit_message: [FLINK-35702][parquet] support parquet read nested in nested (#24991)
patch.improved_commit_message: Refactor Parquet nested structure handling and improve efficiency of Row and Map reading functionalities.
patch.change_summary: This commit introduces significant improvements to the handling of nested structures within Parquet files. It simplifies the process of reading nested arrays and maps while ensuring better type safety and performance. Additionally, a new utility has been added to maintain the positional context when working with nested rows and collections. Various tests have been added to validate the changes made.
hints: Removed redundant code for reading nested rows; consolidated into a unified approach.
Introduced specialized classes to streamline parsing and processing of nested collections.
Updated the ColumnReader interface for consistent behavior across different types.
Utilized strong typing and type checks to improve the robustness of the read operations.
Added comprehensive unit tests for newly introduced functionality to ensure correctness.

+
+import java.util.function.Predicate;
+
+/**
+ * A Collection of useful {@link Condition}s for {@link TypeSerializer} and {@link
+ * TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility}.
+ */
+public final class TypeSerializerConditions {
+
+    private TypeSerializerConditions() {}
+
+    public static <T> Condition<TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility<T>> isCompatibleAsIs() {
+        return new Condition<>(
+                TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility::isCompatibleAsIs,
+                "type serializer schema that is a compatible as is");
+    }
+
+    public static <T> Condition<TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility<T>> isIncompatible() {
+        return new Condition<>(
+                TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility::isIncompatible,
+                "type serializer schema that is incompatible");
+    }
+
+    public static <T> Condition<TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility<T>> isCompatibleAfterMigration() {
+        return new Condition<>(
+                TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility::isCompatibleAfterMigration,
+                "type serializer schema that is compatible after migration");
+    }
+
+    public static <T>
+            Condition<TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility<T>>
+                    isCompatibleWithReconfiguredSerializer() {
+        return new Condition<>(
+                TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility::isCompatibleWithReconfiguredSerializer,
+                "type serializer schema that is compatible with a reconfigured serializer");
+    }
+
+    public static <T>
+            Condition<TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility<T>> isCompatibleWithReconfiguredSerializer(
+                    Predicate<? super TypeSerializer<T>> reconfiguredSerializerMatcher) {
+        return new Condition<>(
+                compatibility ->
+                        compatibility.isCompatibleWithReconfiguredSerializer()
+                                && reconfiguredSerializerMatcher.test(
+                                        compatibility.getReconfiguredSerializer()),
+                "type serializer schema that is compatible with a reconfigured serializer matching "
+                        + reconfiguredSerializerMatcher);
+    }
+
+    public static <T> Condition<TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility<T>> hasSameCompatibilityAs(
+            TypeSerializerSchemaCompatibility<T> expectedCompatibility) {
+        return new Condition<>(
+                actual ->
+                        actual.isCompatibleAsIs() == expectedCompatibility.isCompatibleAsIs()
+                                && actual.isIncompatible() == expectedCompatibility.isIncompatible()
+                                && actual.isCompatibleAfterMigration()
+                                        == expectedCompatibility.isCompatibleAfterMigration()
+                                && actual.isCompatibleWithReconfiguredSerializer()
+                                        == expectedCompatibility
+                                                .isCompatibleWithReconfiguredSerializer(),
+                "same compatibility as " + expectedCompatibility);
+    }
+}

patch.improved_commit_message: Refactor getTransitivePredecessors methods to internal implementation and add caching.
patch.change_summary: This refactoring involves renaming the public method getTransitivePredecessors() to protected getTransitivePredecessorsInternal() across multiple classes in the Flink API. The public method now serves as a wrapper that utilizes a caching mechanism to optimize the retrieval of transitive predecessors. This change enhances performance by reducing repeated computations for previously fetched results, while also better encapsulating the internal logic of the transformation classes.
hints: All calls to getTransitivePredecessors have been updated to use getTransitivePredecessorsInternal.
Introduced a predecessorsCache map to store the results of getTransitivePredecessorsInternal.
Updated the transformation classes such as CacheTransformation, FeedbackTransformation, etc., to implement the internal method instead of the public method.

patch.orig_commit_message:
[FLINK-29114][connector][filesystem] Fix issue of file overwriting caused by multiple writes to the same sink table and shared staging directory

This closes #24390

* Fix unstable TableSourceITCase#testTableHintWithLogicalTableScanReuse
* Moves the staging dir configuration into builder for easier testing

---------

Co-authored-by: Matthias Pohl <matthias.pohl@aiven.io>
patch.improved_commit_message: Refactor filesystem output format to use 'stagingPath' instead of 'tmpPath'
patch.change_summary: This refactor updates the FileSystemOutputFormat class and its Builder to use 'stagingPath' in place of 'tmpPath'. The renaming improves clarity, reflecting the purpose of this path in the context of staging files before they are finalized. Additionally, changes were made in the associated tests to accommodate this updated variable naming.
hints: Renamed method 'setTempPath' to 'setStagingPath'.
Renamed parameter 'tmpPath' to 'stagingPath'.
Renamed attributes 'tmpPath' to 'stagingPath' throughout FileSystemOutputFormat and its Builder.
Updated method calls and checks that utilized 'tmpPath' to now reference 'stagingPath'.
Replaced instances of 'ref' with 'outputFormat' for clarity in test harnesses.

patch.orig_commit_message:
[FLINK-34053][table-planner] Support state ttl hint for group aggregate

This closes #24179
patch.improved_commit_message: Refactor method and variable names for clarity and consistency in hint processing
patch.change_summary: This commit performs a series of renaming refactorings to improve the clarity and consistency of method and variable names across various classes dealing with query hints and relational nodes. Key updates include renaming the `visitBiRel` method to `doVisit`, indicating its purpose more clearly, and standardizing the variable names from `biRel` to `node` and `hBiRel` to `hNode` to reflect generic usage.
hints: Renamed method 'visitBiRel' to 'doVisit' for clarity in purpose.
Updated variable name from 'hBiRel' to 'hNode' in relevant methods to indicate more generic use.
Changed parameter naming from 'biRel' to 'node' for better abstraction.
Consistently renamed parameters and method calls across classes to reflect the changes, ensuring a unified approach to relational node handling.
Updated test methods to reflect renamed methods for validity and clarity in hint-based tests.

patch.orig_commit_message: [FLINK-34204][core] Dispatch legacy serializer related methods in ExecutionConfig to SerializerConfig
patch.improved_commit_message: Refactor Serialization Classes and Configuration to Use SerializerConfigImpl
patch.change_summary: This commit renames and updates various classes, methods, and variables to improve the naming conventions and clarity around serializer configurations in the Flink API. The primary change involves the renaming of 'ExecutionConfig' references to 'SerializerConfig' and the introduction of 'SerializerConfigImpl' to centralize serialization configuration.
hints: Renamed 'ExecutionConfig' to 'SerializerConfig' throughout the codebase to clarify purpose.
Created 'SerializerConfigImpl' to implement 'SerializerConfig' interface, replacing direct usages of 'ExecutionConfig' where applicable.
Updated method signatures and internal variable names across multiple classes to reflect the new serializer configuration structure.
Revised unit tests to accommodate renamed classes and methods, ensuring they now utilize 'SerializerConfigImpl' for configurations.

patch.orig_commit_message:
[FLINK-28915][k8s] Support fetching remote job jar and additional dependencies on Kubernetes

Closes #24065.
patch.improved_commit_message: Refactor artifact fetching mechanism and improve related configurations
patch.change_summary: This commit includes significant refactorings across multiple classes in the Flink project to enhance the artifact fetching process. Key changes include renaming methods and parameters for clarity, modifying the way artifacts are handled when deploying applications, and implementing support for passing multiple JAR files to simplify artifact management.
hints: Renamed methods and parameters for better clarity, e.g., 'getClasspathsFromUserLibDir' to 'getClasspathsFromArtifacts'.
Updated to allow multiple JARs in configurations, enhancing flexibility.
Standardized the naming convention for method parameters related to user artifacts.
Reorganized artifact fetching logic into 'ArtifactFetchManager' to centralize the fetching process.
Created new result handling for fetching jar and additional artifacts.
